title: Slow Cooker Beef, Potato & Pea Stew
description: A simple slow-cooker stew with tender beef, potatoes, carrots, and peas using ordinary grocery-store ingredients.
substitutions: Use baby carrots cut in half instead of sliced carrots.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.

steps.text: Put the beef, potatoes, carrots, and broth in the slow cooker.
Cook until tender, then stir in peas.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds beef stew meat, 1 1/2 pounds potatoes, 3 sliced carrots, 3 cups beef broth, and 1 teaspoon garlic powder if using into the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 7 hours, until the beef and potatoes are tender.
Stir in 1 cup frozen peas, cover, and cook 10 more minutes until the peas are hot.
Taste, season with salt and pepper as needed, and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming hot.

title: Sheet-Pan Turkey Meatballs, Broccoli & Potatoes
description: Premade turkey meatballs roast with potatoes and broccoli for a low-effort dinner with almost no cleanup.
substitutions: Use chicken meatballs instead of turkey meatballs.
Use cauliflower florets instead of broccoli.
Use sweet potato cubes instead of white potatoes.

steps.text: Add meatballs and broccoli and roast until hot and tender.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 pound quartered potatoes with 2 teaspoons of the oil and spread them on a large sheet pan.
Add 12 ounces cooked turkey meatballs and 4 cups broccoli. Toss the broccoli with the remaining 1 teaspoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using.
Roast everything 12–15 minutes more, until the potatoes and broccoli are tender and the meatballs are steaming hot.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat until the meatballs are steaming hot.

title: Leftover Rice, Egg & Cheddar Cups
description: Leftover rice, eggs, and cheddar bake into savory little cups for breakfast, lunch, or a snackable dinner.

ingredients.item: oil or cooking spray for pan

substitutions: Use cooked quinoa instead of rice.
Use chopped cooked broccoli instead of peas.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Mix the leftover rice with eggs and cheese.
Bake in muffin cups until set.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease 6 muffin cups with 1 teaspoon oil or cooking spray.
In a bowl, mix 1 1/2 cups cold cooked rice, 4 eggs, 3/4 cup shredded cheddar, and 1/2 cup thawed peas if using.
Divide the mixture evenly among the 6 prepared muffin cups.
Bake 18–20 minutes, until the centers are set and the edges are lightly golden.
Cool 5 minutes, loosen the edges, and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot. Use rice that was cooled promptly and kept refrigerated.

title: Small-Batch Cinnamon Toast Bread Pudding
description: A small pan of cozy cinnamon bread pudding turns a few slices of stale sandwich bread into dessert for two.
substitutions: Use brioche or leftover rolls instead of sandwich bread.
Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Add 2 tablespoons raisins if you like them.

steps.text: Soak the stale bread in cinnamon custard.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a small baking dish. Put 3 slices cubed stale bread in the dish.
Whisk 1 egg, 1/2 cup milk, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla if using.
Pour the custard over the bread, press the bread down gently, and let it stand 5 minutes.
Bake 22–25 minutes, until the center is set and the top is lightly browned.
Cool a few minutes and serve warm.

storage: Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days and reheat until warm. Do not leave the finished custard dessert at room temperature for extended periods.
